name: Liadan

attributes.attribute: a bard from the province of Munster
declined the poet Cuirithir and then grieved
became a priest and was later cast out

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Liadan is an Irish heroine and a bard. She came from Munster, the part of Ireland most tied to music and song. The poet Cuirithir loved her while he walked his circuit of the island. She declined him and asked that he come to her home in County Kerry. He never came, so she entered a convent and then grieved. Later she found he had become a priest. That put an end to any hope of union. When Cuirithir was cast out for seeking her, she died of grief at his praying stone. The tale is Christian, but it keeps older Celtic themes of a woman poet and a test of true love.

okr.objective: Tell the bard Liadan and her sad bond with Cuirithir in a short source-true form.
key_results: Give her home province and what made her a bard.
Describe how Cuirithir lost her and why.
